//: Lighthouse CI budgets (plan/01 §7, spec 004 AC-24). JSON has no comments, so this key is the
note; `@lhci/cli` reads `.ci` and ignores everything beside it.
`resource-summary:script:size` is **transfer** size, i.e. the bytes on the wire after content
encoding. Vercel serves Brotli, so 122 880 here means 120 KB Brotli — which is what spec 004
§13 Q13 restated the plan/01 §7 budget as (founder decision, 2026-09-08, option (a)), and what
`pnpm budget:client-js` now compares against. Before that restatement this number was read as
gzip in the repository and as Brotli by Lighthouse, and the same build was 'over' or 'under'
depending on the reader.
Reconciled against this PR's own preview run (`/review 26` item 5), because 'transfer size'
and 'our JavaScript' are not the same set. Lighthouse measured `/` at 141 769 B; a browser
fetching the same preview downloads 116 393 B of our chunks (Brotli, every `.js` the page
requests). The 25 376 B difference is the platform's `vercel.live` feedback script, which is
injected into protected previews, is absent from production and is not in our build output.
So the encoding matches — Lighthouse's number and a Brotli sum of our chunks agree to within
the third-party script — and the assertion is comparable to 122 880 only on a URL with no
platform script, i.e. production. On a locale document `vercel.live` costs far more (the
same run read 249 766 B for `/en` against 200 900 B of our chunks at the time, ~48 KB of it
platform script), which is why `lighthouse` stays `continue-on-error` here: TASK-056 owns
both the enforcement flip and the decision of where to measure it (production URLs, or a
first-party-only budget) so that the number it blocks on is the number this repository can
change.
`categories:seo` is collected but deliberately **not** asserted: every page in Phase 0 is
`noindex` (ADR-0007, spec 001 §6), so the SEO category would score the robots directive rather
than the page, and nobody should be able to make a number green by indexing early. Spec 007
asserts it when there is an indexable set. AC-24 (TASK-056) owns the enforcement flip and the
five-URL set; TASK-046 owns these numbers being achievable.
